cards.explanation: The answer is the Holy Spirit. Matthew says Mary "…was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit." (Matthew 1:18). Later the angel says it again, that the One conceived in her "…is from the Holy Spirit." (Matthew 1:20). Same source both times, friends, and it's not a surprise to heaven.

The word is divorce. Matthew 1:19 says Joseph "…resolved to divorce her quietly." The text tells us he was a righteous man and unwilling to disgrace Mary publicly. I think he was trying to walk a very narrow road with a very heavy heart, friends.

It happens in a dream. Matthew says "…an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream…" (Matthew 1:20). Joseph had been pondering, and then the message came while he slept. Most of my best ideas come when I'm asleep too, bakers, but mine are about cookie shapes.

The answer is False. Joseph had resolved to divorce Mary quietly, but the angel says, "…do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife…" (Matthew 1:20). The angel gives the reason too: the One conceived in her "…is from the Holy Spirit." So the angel doesn't tell him to go ahead, friends. He tells him to embrace Mary as his wife.

The reason is that He will save His people from their sins. The angel says, "…you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins." (Matthew 1:21). The reason for the name is right there in the same sentence, friends. That's what the name is about, straight from the angel.

The word is virgin. The words say, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son…" (Matthew 1:23). Matthew tells us these words come from the prophet, and the Lord said them through him. Lean in on that one, bakers.

Immanuel means God with us. The text says they will call Him Immanuel "(which means, 'God with us')" (Matthew 1:23). Matthew gives us the meaning himself, right in the verse. Read that name slowly, friends. It's a good one to sit with.

When Joseph wakes up, he embraces Mary as his wife. Matthew says that when Joseph woke up, "…he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and embraced Mary as his wife." (Matthew 1:24). The text doesn't mention any delay, bakers. He heard the word, and he did it.
